targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.blurb: The fastest-moving star in our sky (about 10.4 arcseconds per year), 6 light-years away. SPHEREx sees it shift by 1–2 pixels between 2025 and 2026.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.blurb: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi, 12 light-years away. Brown dwarfs are too small to shine like stars but glow in the infrared.

targets.name: WISE 0855−0714
targets.blurb: The coldest brown dwarf known, about 7 light-years away. It is extremely faint at short wavelengths and is expected to show up only in SPHEREx's longest-wavelength detectors.

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.blurb: A young star system whose brightness changes irregularly, partly because dust passes in front of it.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.blurb: A Mira-type pulsating giant star that brightens and fades over about 245 days.

targets.name: Proxima Centauri
targets.blurb: The closest star to the Sun (4.2 light-years), a small red dwarf with planets. It moves about 3.9″ per year.

targets.name: Kapteyn's Star
targets.blurb: An old red star 13 light-years away that orbits our galaxy the 'wrong' way. It moves about 8.7″ per year — the second-fastest star.

targets.name: 3I/ATLAS (Aug 2025)
targets.blurb: The third known interstellar object. It moves across the sky within hours, so single SPHEREx exposures from one day already show it travelling past the stars. Positions are IRSA predictions, not detections.
